Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first map the workspace contract and inspect both rollout views, then use the fish-control bookshelf to form one mechanism-level candidate. I’m using `read-wake-visual-signals-first` because this policy change depends on the two visual wake views, followed by the explicitly requested `fish-control-primitives` transfer protocol.

The workspace requires a pre-edit visual diagnosis and forbids running CFD locally. I’ve confirmed the experiment is the direct still-water, no-cylinder lane; next I’m anchoring the candidate to the inherited guidance, all sampled scores/metrics, and the best-versus-failure keyframe comparison before touching the policy.

The visual comparison is consistent and useful: both candidates self-propel with a coherent alternating 3D wake, but the inherited prefill reaches a much closer pass (`2.319L`) and then executes a large late turn that carries it away; the highest-score sample stays on a straighter, high-side path and exits earlier with a worse closest pass (`4.650L`). I’m now isolating which approach mechanism caused those trajectory differences and checking its actuation/geometry traces before committing to a single translation.

The shelf consultation points to one clean transfer: closed-loop course modulation of an existing rhythmic carrier. I’m adopting only the invariant—steer the preserved traveling bend from sensed target/velocity alignment—not any published gains or route. The candidate will replace the unsuccessful terminal carrier-braking branch with a rotation-invariant body-frame course-error command; this directly tests whether earlier, phase-robust interception can improve the `2.319L` near miss without the joint pinning seen in the approach schedulers.

The candidate now passes syntax, bounded-action, and reflection-equivariance checks. Its key safety property also holds structurally: with full carrier retained and asymmetry capped below one, steering cannot reverse the oscillator’s restorative half-cycle—the failure mode that let the approach schedulers settle against joint limits. I’m checking command effort on all four recorded trajectories next, then I’ll distill the reusable negative/positive boundary into inherited guidance.

The recorded-state replay exposed a real safety problem before CFD: removing all approach relief raised near-target command-cap occupancy from `36.1%` to `86.4%` on the prefill trace. I’m refining the same course-error mechanism so the near-target gate scales the complete carrier-plus-asymmetry command together. That preserves course correction, slows a predicted miss, and guarantees the steering term cannot overpower the restorative half-cycle. This refinement is driven by the dry evidence and stays within the bookshelf’s “preserve the rhythm, modulate it from feedback” invariant.

The reusable guidance is now materially updated with the sampled boundary: carrier-only relief produced the closest pass but joint pinning; bend release fixed pinning/load without fixing interception; joint-angle phase separation improved score while degrading the pass. The durable implication is to evaluate terminal geometry and co-scale rhythmic drive/steering, with course feedback valid only once velocity is reliable. I’m now invoking all three checks prescribed by `.codex/agents/check-runner.toml` separately.

The first prescribed check found a rendered-workspace defect rather than a candidate defect: `README.md` marks the same assigned guidance parent twice, so the checker counts two copied parents. I’m inspecting the checker interface; if it has no explicit-parent override, I’ll remove only the duplicated marker so the required semantic comparison can run.

All prescribed checks now pass: guidance semantic change, exact multi-wake policy contract, and solver boundary. The only repair outside the requested artifacts was removing the duplicated assigned-parent marker in the rendered `README.md`, which was preventing the mandated guidance check from identifying a unique parent. I’m doing a final schema/content audit now; no CFD will be run.

Implemented exactly one course-error target-policy candidate.

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl): rotation-invariant target/velocity course feedback with co-scaled near-miss slowdown.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md): visual diagnosis, evidence, bookshelf transfer block, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:66): reusable terminal-scheduling lesson.

All prescribed checks pass: guidance semantics, policy contract, parameter schema, reflection symmetry, bounded actions, and solver boundary. Dry replay reduced near-target above-95%-cap occupancy from `36.1%` to `15.1%`. Formal CFD was intentionally not run.
